title: Find water
summary: Water runs downhill: check low ground, the foot of cliffs and dry stream beds.

list: Water runs downhill. Check valley bottoms and other low ground, the foot of cliffs or rocks, and dry stream beds; dig on the outside of bends.

blocks.cap: Dig on the outside of a bend in a dry stream bed. If you hit wet sand, dig down into it and let water seep in.

list: Signs of water nearby: lush green vegetation, swarming insects, game trails that meet in a V, and birds flying in the early morning or late afternoon, which may show the direction to water.
Catch rain on a tarp, poncho or large leaves.
Before sunrise, tie absorbent cloth around your ankles, walk through tall grass, and wring out the dew.
Tie a clear plastic bag over a leafy branch of a non-poisonous plant in full sun and seal it. Water collects in the bag as the leaves breathe.

blocks.cap: A transpiration bag. Collect the water before sundown. The same branch can be used for 3 to 5 days. The water tastes like the plant smells.

list: Skip lake or pond water that is strongly colored, looks like paint or has floating scum: it may be a harmful algal bloom, and treating it yourself does not make it safe (see Make water safe).
Treat all wild water, rain included, before drinking (see Make water safe).

sources.name: US Army ATP 3-50.21, Survival (2018), chapter 3 (Table 3-1, paragraphs 3-2, 3-11, 3-15, 3-27, 3-34)
sources.used: Seepage wells at outside bends of a dry riverbed and the foot of cliffs or rocks; dig deep enough for water to seep in; rain on nonporous items, rain off leaves; dew with cloth around the lower legs; transpiration bag sealed over a leafy branch, collect before sundown, same limb 3 or 5 days; do not drink saltwater or urine

sources.name: US Army FM 21-76-1, Survival, Evasion, and Recovery (1999), chapter VII
sources.used: Water indicators: lush green vegetation, drainages and low-lying areas, V-intersecting game trails, swarming insects, bird flight in early morning or late afternoon; transpiration bag must be clear, no poisonous plants, water tastes like the plant smells; do not drink urine or sea water

sources.name: US Army FM 21-76, Survival Manual, chapter 6
sources.used: Dew: rags around the ankles, walk through dew-covered grass before sunrise

sources.name: City of Phoenix Fire Department, Desert survival
sources.used: Base of rock cliffs; dig at the outside edge of a sharp bend in a dry stream bed; dig into wet sand for seeping water

sources.name: CDC, How to Find Clean Water in an Emergency
sources.used: Rainwater, streams, rivers, ponds, lakes and springs must be treated to kill germs

sources.name: New York State Department of Health, Harmful Blue-Green Algae Blooms
sources.used: Bloom appearance; do not drink surface water during a bloom even if you treat it yourself
